status_summary: No order, notice or law ending the Clean Energy Corps, its funding or the positions filled under it was found. DOE's former Corps web address now leads to a general careers page, last modified 2026-04-16, that does not mention the program. In parallel, the Federation of American Scientists reported on 2026-07-28 that DOE lost over 2,700 federal staff, mostly through the 2025 deferred resignation program, and that science and energy innovation offices lost an estimated 43 percent of federal employees by October 2025. Bloomberg Government reported on 2025-10-15 that layoff notices went to staff in four DOE offices including renewable energy and clean energy demonstrations. None of these sources names the Corps.

timeline.event: DOE's former Clean Energy Corps web address resolves to a general careers page, last modified that day, that does not mention the program.

title: Eliminate the DOE Clean Energy Corps and its positions
uncertainties: Searched the web for news naming the Clean Energy Corps in 2025 and 2026 and found no source stating it was ended; the October 2025 layoff notices were issued during a shutdown and their later status was not traced. The careers page was first published in 2024, so when the Corps address began redirecting is unknown. Systematic checks of the Federal Register, Unified Agenda and congress.gov were not completed, so this not_started finding rests on limited search.
